m:tromost: Free to walk around at any hour. The square is closed to traffic. In the evening it's lit up and it's the best place for a photo.
m:vecchio: Free to walk around. The shops close early and many stay closed on Sundays; the riverside bars stay open into the evening. The old town is pedestrian.
m:mercato: The market is open Monday to Saturday, normally from 6am to 6pm (Saturday until 4pm, in winter it closes earlier, to be confirmed), and closed on Sundays. The Cathedral can be visited for free outside services (hours not checked: to be confirmed). From autumn the stalls are packed up in the evening.
m:castello: Open every day, normally from 9am to 9pm in winter (last entry half an hour before): the sources I read disagree on hours and prices, so check ljubljanskigrad.si. Prices from guides: castle entry €13–15, with a return funicular about €19; funicular only €6 return (to be confirmed). The funicular leaves from Krekov trg, near the market. The courtyard is free to visit.
m:crociera: Adult ticket €15.82, children aged 6–13 €8.44, under 6 free (visitljubljana.com). Departs from the Breg 1 pier. I couldn't find the times or whether trips run in autumn and winter: check the calendar on the Visit Ljubljana website and book online.
m:tivoli: The park is always open and free to visit. The nicest stretch is the long Jakopič promenade, with open-air photo exhibitions. It's about a 15-minute walk from Prešeren Square.
m:congressi: The square is free to visit at any hour; the library can be seen from outside (I couldn't find hours for visiting inside: to be confirmed).
vd:nobel: The burek kiosk: flaky pastry filled with cheese or meat, typical of the Balkans and of a Ljubljana breakfast. Eaten hot, often with a glass of yoghurt. Open day and night.
vp:nobel: A burek costs €2–4 (range from guides, menu not seen). Hours from an online listing, to be confirmed.
vd:klobasarna: A small deli-tavern near the Cathedral serving kranjska klobasa, the Carniolan sausage, with mustard and horseradish, and hot dishes like jota, the sauerkraut soup, and ričet, the barley soup.
vp:klobasarna: A dish usually costs €4–10 (menu not seen). Hours from an online listing, to be confirmed.
vd:sokol: A restaurant in rustic rooms decorated in traditional style, with waiters in costume and Slovenian dishes: soups, roasts, grilled meat and house desserts, with a good list of Slovenian wines.
vp:sokol: A main course is around €12–20 (estimate, menu not seen). Hours from an online listing, to be confirmed.
vd:druga: A restaurant in the old town where people with disabilities also work: simple Slovenian cooking, with beef noodle soup, kranjska klobasa and štruklji (rolled dumplings, sweet or savoury).
vp:druga: A dish is around €6–10 (range from guides, menu not seen). Hours from Visit Ljubljana; it appears to be closed on Mondays, but the listing doesn't say so explicitly: to be confirmed.
vd:ribca: A small fish shop-restaurant on the riverbank, with fresh fish, squid and prawns bought at the fish market next door. It has a fixed-price lunch menu of the day.
vp:ribca: The lunch menu costs about €10.50; other fish dishes €8–14 (from guides, to be confirmed). Hours from an online listing, to be confirmed.
vd:sestica: One of the city's oldest restaurants, since 1776: traditional Slovenian dishes like jota and kranjska klobasa, served by waiters in costume, and prekmurska gibanica, a layered cake of poppy seeds, walnuts, apples and cottage cheese.
vp:sestica: A main course is around €12–18 (estimate, menu not seen). Hours from Visit Ljubljana.
vd:zvezda: A bright café popular with students and locals, a short walk from Congress Square, with strong coffee, cakes and ice cream. It's a little pricier than average.
vp:zvezda: A coffee with a cake is around €7–10 (estimate, menu not seen). Hours from an online listing, to be confirmed.
cd:nazionale: The country's history, with the Neanderthal flute and the marshland wheel.
cd:cittamuseo: Two thousand years of city life, from Roman Emona to today.
cd:zoolj: A zoo on a wooded hill, close to the centre.
cd:moderna: 20th-century Slovenian art in a building near Tivoli.
cd:plecnik: The home of the architect who designed Ljubljana, preserved as it was.
